clue.text: Container left by rail

parts.note: a barre is the handrail dancers hold in ballet practice

explanation.surface: A shipping box abandoned beside a railway line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' just puts the two pieces side by side, the ballet rail first.
explanation.definitionFit: A cask or drum for holding liquids is a straightforward kind of container.

clue.text: Lost ground to Queen's horseman

indicators.note: ground is the past participle of grind, so the letters of the word before it are milled into a new order

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual abbreviation for the Queen

explanation.surface: A rider surrenders territory to the monarch's cavalryman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' looks like land lost in battle, but it is the past tense of grind, signalling an anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: An inn's stableman who looked after guests' horses was a horseman of a humble kind.

clue.text: Landing plane totally empty

parts.note: a jet is a kind of aircraft

indicators.note: emptying a word removes its insides, leaving only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: An aircraft touches down with nobody aboard at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Landing' looks like the plane's arrival but is a noun: a place where boats land.
explanation.definitionFit: A pier where boats moor and passengers come ashore is a landing stage.

clue.text: Move in or suffer (he'll take in all sorts)

indicators.note: the words before it are made to suffer, knocked about into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An invitation to move in or endure hardship, with a note about a tolerant host.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracketed words read like an aside about a broad-minded landlord, but they define an eater of plants and meat alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A creature that eats both animal and vegetable food consumes every kind of thing.

clue.text: Junior staff sacked mostly — you beast!

indicators.note: sacked suggests being pillaged or turned over, so the letters are thrown into disorder
mostly keeps all but the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A boss fires the office juniors and hurls an insult at one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims YOU to YO; 'sacked' then reorders YO and BEAST.
explanation.definitionFit: Lads who once made tea in offices were the lowliest employees, a byword for junior workers.

clue.text: Not yet prepared to accept criminal leaving east — hard to blame him

indicators.note: the shuffled letters take in the next piece, holding it inside them
prepared means made up or worked into shape, so these letters are rearranged
leaving shows a letter departs from the word

parts.note: a felon is a person guilty of a serious crime
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A suspect not yet ready to take in a criminal, though no one can pin anything on him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not yet' rearranged gives TETONY, which takes in FLON (FELON without E). Tony Blair earned this nickname because scandal never seemed to stick to him.
explanation.definitionFit: The nickname says, like a non-stick pan coating, nothing would adhere to Blair, so faulting him was difficult.

clue.text: Obvious the setter's on drugs, meaning extra work

parts.note: overt means open and plain to see
the setter speaking of himself says I'm, so this gives IM
E is slang for ecstasy, the drug

explanation.surface: Someone notes that the crossword compiler is plainly high, implying he is doing additional hours.
explanation.definitionFit: Hours worked beyond the normal schedule are additional labour, usually paid at a higher rate.

clue.text: Agent on duty finally getting caught — he's not very bright

indicators.note: the agent catches the following letters, holding them inside

parts.note: a G-man is an American FBI agent
on in the sense of concerning, as is RE

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A spy on assignment is finally arrested, which suggests he was rather dim.
explanation.walkthrough: John Major was nicknamed the grey man for his supposedly colourless personality; 'bright' means vivid, not clever.
explanation.definitionFit: A dull, colourless figure lacks vividness, and that drabness was the gibe aimed at Major.

clue.text: I admitted to saying horse and carriage

indicators.note: the letter is let into the middle of the other piece
saying means the word is spoken, here written as its two letter-names G G

parts.note: gee-gee is the nursery word for a horse

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to calling out the names of a horse and its carriage.
explanation.walkthrough: Gee-gee, said as letters, is GG; 'admitted to' puts I inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A light two-wheeled vehicle drawn by one horse is a type of carriage.

clue.text: Japanese city lifted an artist

indicators.note: lifted, in a down clue, raises the little word so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: Francisco Goya was the Spanish painter

explanation.surface: A city in Japan elevated the reputation of a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifted' looks like praise for the painter; in a down clue it means read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a major industrial city on Honshu, the main island of Japan.

clue.text: Will broadcaster co-operate finally? Don King fight could be Sky feature

indicators.note: could be says the letters may be rearranged into something else
finally takes the last letter of each of the three words before it

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a satellite broadcaster will agree to screen a boxing bout promoted by Don King.
explanation.walkthrough: Don King is a famous American boxing promoter, and Sky the British satellite TV channel; here sky is literally the heavens.
explanation.definitionFit: A jagged, branching streak of lightning is something seen in a stormy sky.

clue.text: Look back over bridgehead, repeat and destroy

indicators.note: over means covering, so one piece goes round the other
back reads the word from end to start

parts.note: lo means look, as in lo and behold
the head of the word bridge is its first letter
to iterate is to repeat

explanation.surface: Instructions to review a military foothold, go again and then wipe it out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Look back' gives OL, which sits over (around) B from 'bridgehead'.
explanation.definitionFit: To wipe something out completely, leaving no trace, is to annihilate it.

clue.text: Can get into area

indicators.note: area marks the stretch of the clue's words in which the letters are found

explanation.surface: Permission to enter a zone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can' looks like a verb of permission; it is the noun, a container.
explanation.definitionFit: A metal food container is called this in Britain, just as Americans say a can.

clue.text: See 5
This makes bone doctor go to see Hunt — basic accommodation lacking

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so these letters are altered in order
lacking means the following thing is removed

parts.note: a hut is a simple, basic shelter

explanation.surface: A medic visits Jeremy Hunt, the health secretary, who lacks basic housing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' looks like the person but is the anagram signal; HUNT without HUT leaves N.
explanation.definitionFit: A substance from which bone tissue develops is literally a bone-producer, from Greek osteon (bone) and -gen.

clue.text: Proper artist tries out position of 5 here

parts.note: prim means proper and formal
Tracey Emin is the British artist

indicators.note: out means wrong or disordered, so the word's letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A respectable painter tests a role.
explanation.walkthrough: 5 is Teflon Tony (Blair); 'here' points to the whole puzzle, whose nicknames all belong to holders of this office.
explanation.definitionFit: Blair headed the UK government from 1997 to 2007, the office every nickname in this grid refers to.

clue.text: Belief there's a lot of cover in area

indicators.note: in places the trimmed cover inside the area

parts.note: a region is an area

indicators.note: a lot of means most, dropping the word's last letter

parts.note: a lid is a cover

explanation.surface: A conviction that a large part of the district has protection.
explanation.definitionFit: A faith or creed is a system of belief.

clue.text: Old bird — grouse — losing tail

indicators.note: losing tail drops the word's last letter

parts.note: to grouse is to complain, or moan

explanation.surface: An aged gamebird missing its tail feathers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grouse' sits beside 'bird' to look like the gamebird; here it is a verb meaning complain.
explanation.definitionFit: A huge flightless bird of New Zealand, extinct for centuries, is an old bird in every sense.

clue.text: Expressionless speaker, one upset by breaking word to Barnier?

indicators.note: the pieces break into the French word, sitting inside it

parts.note: Michel Barnier is French, and mot is French for word
A means one

indicators.note: upset turns the little word on its head

parts.note: taken as written before being turned

explanation.surface: A wooden-faced orator is put out by a message to the EU's Brexit negotiator.
explanation.walkthrough: BY upside down is YB. Theresa May was nicknamed this for her robotic delivery; Michel Barnier led Brexit talks for the EU.
explanation.definitionFit: The nickname blends her surname with robot, mocking a stiff, mechanical, emotionless speaking style.

clue.text: Spirit of 11, say

indicators.note: say signals the word is spoken, giving one spelt differently

parts.note: the answer to 11 down is an example of a metal

explanation.surface: Asking about the spirit of another clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' does double service, marking 11 as an example and the word as heard.
explanation.definitionFit: Courage and resilience are both spirit and grit.

clue.text: No-pressure friendly for supporter

indicators.note: No means the following thing is absent

parts.note: pally is informal for friendly
P is the abbreviation for pressure in physics

explanation.surface: A relaxed friendly match for a fan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No-pressure friendly' looks like a casual football game; it is PALLY minus P.
explanation.definitionFit: A partner who backs you up in a cause is a supporter.

clue.text: See everyone has money and avoid going back (I'm just one of the lads)

definitions.text: I'm just one of the lads

parts.note: the letter C is pronounced see, a stock crossword equivalence
all means everyone

indicators.note: going back reads the word from its end

parts.note: to evade is to avoid

explanation.surface: A wheeler-dealer's advice about a crowd with cash, ending with a matey aside about being ordinary.
explanation.walkthrough: EVADE backwards gives EDAVE. David Cameron invited informality with this phrase, which became his nickname.
explanation.definitionFit: Asking to be called by a chummy short name is a way of claiming to be an ordinary bloke.

clue.text: Got a supply of City papers at home

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles
ID means identity papers
in means at home

explanation.surface: Someone acquired a stock of financial newspapers to read at home.
explanation.definitionFit: To stock up on provisions for future use is to lay them in.

clue.text: As arms may be first on agenda, tyrant starts to back off

indicators.note: first on picks the opening letter of the word that follows

parts.note: Kim Jong-un is the North Korean dictator

indicators.note: starts to picks the first letters of the next two words

explanation.surface: Weapons top the summit agenda as a despot begins to retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arms' looks military, as in weapons; here they are limbs.
explanation.definitionFit: Hands on hips with elbows out is a stance in which a person's limbs are held.

clue.text: Plain element of personal life's been raised

indicators.note: raised, in a down clue, reads the letters upward
element of means only part of the words is taken

explanation.surface: Part of someone's private life has come to light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plain' looks like an adjective, but it is a noun: an open grassland.
explanation.definitionFit: A treeless grassy expanse in South America, Spanish for flat ground, is a plain.

clue.text: Duke with power smashed 'Fight Club' — no hearts sinking

indicators.note: smashed means broken to pieces, so these letters are put together again differently
no means the following letter is missing

parts.note: H is the card abbreviation for hearts

explanation.surface: An aristocrat with clout wrecks a film, and the heartless violence sinks it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duke' looks like a nobleman; dukes is slang for fists. Gordon Brown was called this after Tony Blair's reported remark.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong man's hand clenched as a weapon is literally a mighty fist, nicknaming the forceful Gordon Brown.

clue.text: Want day out as previously referred to

indicators.note: out means removed from the word

parts.note: to want is to need

explanation.surface: A wish for a free day, as mentioned before.
explanation.definitionFit: Placed before a maiden name, this French word marks what someone was formerly called.

clue.text: Beat easily — right-back's a lightweight

indicators.note: back turns the abbreviation around

parts.note: an ounce is a small unit of weight

explanation.surface: A football team wins comfortably, though its right-back is a featherweight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right-back' looks like the football position; it is RT reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: To thrash an opponent is to win by a wide margin.

clue.text: Base in one French city about to go

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one

indicators.note: to go means the following piece is dropped

parts.note: Grenoble is a city in the French Alps
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Someone sets up headquarters in a French city, about to leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Base' looks like a headquarters; it is an adjective meaning dishonourable.
explanation.definitionFit: Base and dishonourable both mean lacking moral worth.
